name: Grace Minseo Han

residence.living_arrangement: Lives alone in a small apartment. After sharing with roommates in her twenties, she chose a place of her own because she likes setting her own routines and having a quiet space to return to.

gross_household_income: $148,000 annually. Her household has one person, so this is also her own gross income.

education.background: Studied information science at a public university in Washington and completed her degree in her early twenties.
education.approach: She liked the practical side of the subject: how people find information, where interfaces confuse them, and how small design decisions can make a tool easier or harder to use. She still reads and learns on her own, though she does not treat every interest as a career project.

long_term_goals: Keep building expertise in product accessibility and have a meaningful say in how products are designed, without moving into a management role solely for status.
Maintain enough financial flexibility to handle emergencies, take trips, and make housing decisions at her own pace.
Keep close relationships with family and friends while protecting time that is genuinely her own.
Explore international travel at some point, but she has no particular destination or arrangement settled.

occupation.title: Product accessibility specialist
occupation.work: She turns user feedback and accessibility concerns into practical changes to digital products. Her work involves explaining problems clearly to product and design colleagues, reviewing proposed fixes, and following up to see whether changes work in practice.
occupation.work_history: After studying information science, she started in product-related support and quality work and gradually moved toward accessibility. She has spent about a decade developing experience in technology roles.
occupation.work_rhythm: Her income is steady, but launches and deadlines can make some weeks much busier than others. She is capable of concentrating for long stretches; after a demanding day, she prefers low-key plans rather than more screen time or a crowded social event.

style.speech: Grace speaks plainly and is direct without trying to dominate a conversation. She asks practical follow-up questions when a plan is vague and prefers clear options to polished persuasion. With friends she is more playful, often using dry humor or sending a specific book, café, or walking-route recommendation. When tired, she gets quieter and tends to say what she can manage rather than pretending to be enthusiastic.
style.conversation_habits: She listens for the practical detail that might change a decision: timing, transit, how much walking is involved, or what happens if plans shift. She is not especially fond of small talk that goes on without finding a point of connection.

personality.big_five_scale: The following values are descriptive fictional tendencies on a 1–5 scale, where 1 is low and 5 is high; they are not psychometric test results.

openness.description: Curious about how places and systems work, drawn to design, books, and unfamiliar neighborhoods. She likes trying new things more when she can approach them at her own pace.

conscientiousness.description: Reliable about work commitments and planning the basics, but not interested in optimizing every hour. She may leave leisure plans deliberately loose.

extraversion.description: Enjoys one-to-one time and small gatherings, but needs quiet time alone. She can be animated with people she knows well and reserved in a new group.

agreeableness.description: Considerate and generous with friends, though she will say when she disagrees or when a request does not suit her.

neuroticism.description: Usually steady under ordinary stress. A compressed deadline can make her more tense and withdrawn, but she tends to regain perspective after rest and a change of scene.

personality.general_tendencies: She is observant and independent-minded. She likes knowing how a decision will work in everyday life and is comfortable changing a plan when it stops being enjoyable or useful.

travel.desired_experience: She likes trips that combine a walkable city with nearby green space: museums, cafés, neighborhood bookstores, interesting streets, and the option of a day hike. She enjoys noticing how different districts feel and how people use public spaces.
travel.pace: She prefers a few anchor plans with room to wander. A packed checklist, repeated long transfers, or an itinerary in which every meal and hour is booked makes a trip feel like another deadline.
travel.accommodation_and_logistics: She values a clean, quiet place in a convenient area and wants to understand local transit before she arrives. She will pay attention to the practical trade-offs of location and comfort, but is not looking for luxury for its own sake.
travel.companions: She often enjoys traveling with a close friend, especially someone who likes walking and can make decisions without turning every choice into a negotiation. She is also comfortable taking a few days alone when schedules do not align.
travel.future_interest: She is interested in international travel and in seeing places beyond the familiar, but has not chosen a destination or made arrangements.

preferences.reading: Enjoys reading for leisure, especially contemporary fiction and books about cities and design. She likes a novel that gives her a strong sense of place, but also picks up nonfiction when a subject catches her attention. She borrows books from the library and trades recommendations with friends.
preferences.social_time: Prefers a meal, a walk, or a relaxed café catch-up over a loud venue where conversation is difficult. She appreciates having one or two evenings open in a typical week.
preferences.home_and_food: Likes a calm, functional home and simple dinners she can make without much fuss. She enjoys trying a café or restaurant now and then, but does not need every free evening to be an outing.

beliefs.political_outlook: Prioritizes individual liberty and is skeptical of government restrictions in both social and economic life. She is wary of rules that intrude on personal choices or create cumbersome processes, and tends to ask whether a proposed restriction is necessary and workable. Her views are sincerely held but are not the subject of every conversation.
beliefs.personal_values: Values privacy, self-direction, competence, and being treated as an adult. She respects people who make different choices for themselves and expects the same latitude in return.

skills: Translating user feedback into specific, actionable product changes.
Noticing where instructions, interfaces, or processes leave people confused or excluded.
Explaining technical or design concerns in clear, practical language.
Planning travel logistics without needing to schedule every moment.
Finding useful books, cafés, and walking routes through recommendations and her own research.

behaviors.daily_routine: When her calendar allows, she takes a walk or goes to a neighborhood gym before work. She cooks uncomplicated dinners, keeps some evenings unscheduled, and reads before bed to get away from screens. During deadline-heavy stretches, exercise and reading are more likely to become shorter or less regular rather than disappearing from her routine altogether.
behaviors.social_routine: She makes a point of seeing friends and family, but does not accept every invitation automatically. She is more likely to suggest a simple plan than to wait for someone else to organize an elaborate one.
behaviors.travel_in_practice: Her paid time off is adequate for one longer trip and a couple of shorter breaks when work and schedules cooperate. She saves for travel while keeping an emergency cushion, and considers time off as well as money when deciding whether a trip feels worthwhile. On a past trip to Vancouver with a close friend, they added an unplanned day to explore on foot rather than squeeze in another booked activity. During a particularly deadline-heavy period, she passed on a proposed long weekend away because she did not want to spend the time worrying about work; she stayed local and used the break to rest and take walks instead.

health.general: She stays active through walking and occasional gym visits, though consistency varies with her work calendar. She has no major health limitation shaping her everyday plans.
health.stress_and_rest: Long stretches of screen work leave her mentally tired. When work piles up she can stay up later than intended, so a quiet evening, a walk, or reading helps her settle down.

relationships.family: She grew up in the Seattle area in a Korean American family. She sees her parents regularly and keeps in touch with a younger cousin; family gatherings matter to her, but she does not regard every gathering as an obligation.
relationships.friends: She has a small circle of close friends, including a friend she has traveled with. She is generous with recommendations and attentive to friends’ practical needs, while being candid when she needs a quieter or simpler plan.
relationships.romantic_and_parenting: She is single, is not currently partnered, and has no children. Her present routines and plans are organized around her own household, work, family, and friendships.

leisure_interests: Reading for pleasure, especially contemporary fiction and books about cities and design.
Taking occasional day hikes and going to the neighborhood gym when her schedule allows.
Traveling, particularly trips that pair an urban setting with access to green space.

other_facts.household_and_finances: She rents and lives alone. Her steady income gives her room to save and travel, but she still weighs discretionary spending against maintaining an emergency cushion.
other_facts.background: She grew up in the Seattle area and has chosen to remain near family and familiar surroundings while building an independent adult life.
